literal: In Liaodong, Yan, Qin, Han, and Tang times prefectures and counties had already been established and offices set.
idiomatic: Liaodong, Yan, and the Qin, Han, and Tang realms had long had prefectures, counties, and officials.

literal: Goryeo and Bohai followed them.
idiomatic: Goryeo and Bohai followed suit.

literal: By Liao, with the five capitals arrayed side by side embracing Yan and Dai, all became metropolitan domains.
idiomatic: Under Liao the five capitals stood in a row, embracing Yan and Dai as the metropolitan heartland.

literal: Over more than two hundred years cities faced one another and fields opened ever wider.
idiomatic: For over two centuries walled towns lined the landscape and farmland spread.

literal: Crowned with military commissioners, continued with observation, defense, and regional training commissioners, and divided among cishi and magistrates—broadly adopting Tang institutions.
idiomatic: Military commissioners headed circuits, observation, defense, and training commissioners followed, and cishi and magistrates filled the counties—largely on the Tang model.

literal: Meanwhile imperial clansmen, maternal kin, and great ministers' households built walled settlements and received designations, called "head-below prefectures and armies";
idiomatic: Imperial kin, in-laws, and great ministers also founded walled estates with granted names—the "head-below prefectures and armies";

literal: only military commissioners were appointed by the court, yet in time they mostly reverted to princely establishments.
idiomatic: only military commissioners were court-appointed, but in time most posts fell to princely households.

literal: Where a prefecture could not be formed it was called an army; where a county could not be formed it was called a city; where a city could not be formed it was called a fort.
idiomatic: Units too small for a prefecture became armies; too small for a county became cities; too small for a city became forts.

literal: Their office establishments are not detailed here.
idiomatic: Their specific offices are not recorded here.

literal: When households went bankrupt and could not supply these duties, common people suffered from it.
idiomatic: Bankrupt households could not meet levies, to the distress of the people.

literal: The office was not regularly established; when there was an edict, an official of talent and standing was chosen for it.
